skill.name: aws-cost-optimizer
skill.description: Analyze AWS spending, identify unused resources, and plan cost reductions with AWS CLI and Cost Explorer guidance.
skill.summary: Find AWS cost drivers and practical optimization actions.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static shell, backtick, and URL findings are false positives from Markdown examples, fixed date substitutions, AWS query syntax, and official AWS links. A semantic risk remains because the skill encourages destructive AWS cleanup actions that need explicit approval, dry-run checks, and backups.

remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only reports and require explicit user approval before any delete, stop, terminate, or rightsizing action.
Frame deletion scripts as review-only drafts and require dry-run support, backup checks, and resource owner validation.
Document least-privilege IAM permissions and warn users before collecting cost, resource, or tag inventory data.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive AWS Resource Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends deleting unattached EBS volumes, deleting old snapshots, stopping or terminating idle EC2 instances, and creating deletion scripts. These actions can cause data loss or service disruption if executed without explicit approval and verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow and prompt examples explicitly include delete, stop, and terminate actions, while the safety notes acknowledge medium and high risk. The skill includes safeguards, so this is operational risk rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: AWS bills can grow from idle resources, weak tagging, and unclear service trends. This skill guides cost reviews, cleanup planning, and savings recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Guides AWS Cost Explorer analysis by service, region, tag, and time period.
Lists AWS CLI checks for unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, and old snapshots.
Provides CloudWatch metric checks for EC2 and RDS rightsizing analysis.
Suggests Savings Plans, Reserved Instance, Spot, and lifecycle policy opportunities.
Outlines a repeatable workflow for baseline assessment, quick wins, and monitoring.
Includes checklist items for budgets, cost allocation tags, anomaly detection, and reviews.
limitations: It depends on AWS CLI access and valid AWS permissions.
It does not verify business ownership of resources before cleanup.
Savings estimates need current pricing and workload context.
Destructive actions require manual approval and rollback planning.

use_cases.title: Monthly AWS Spend Review
use_cases.description: Break down recent AWS costs, compare service trends, and identify the largest drivers for review.

use_cases.title: Idle Resource Cleanup Plan
use_cases.description: Find likely unused volumes, snapshots, Elastic IPs, and idle instances before a controlled cleanup window.

use_cases.title: Executive Savings Report
use_cases.description: Turn cost findings into a prioritized plan with expected savings, risk notes, and approval steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Costs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-optimizer to review my last 30 days of AWS costs by service. Explain the main cost drivers and any unusual increases.

prompt_templates.title: Find Cleanup Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-optimizer to list read-only checks for unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, and old snapshots. Do not delete anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Rightsizing Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-optimizer to compare EC2 and RDS utilization against instance sizes. Recommend rightsizing candidates with risk and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Savings Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-optimizer to create a 90-day AWS savings roadmap. Include quick wins, commitment options, monitoring controls, and approval gates.

output_examples.input: Review AWS costs for the last three months by service.
output_examples.output: A cost summary that ranks top services, explains month-over-month changes, and highlights services that need investigation.

output_examples.input: Find safe cleanup opportunities in my AWS account.
output_examples.output: A read-only checklist of candidate resources, estimated savings areas, validation questions, and approval steps before deletion.

output_examples.input: Create a leadership report for AWS cost reduction.
output_examples.output: An executive summary with savings themes, expected impact ranges, operational risks, owners, and a phased action plan.

best_practices: Start with read-only Cost Explorer and inventory checks before planning changes.
Confirm resource ownership, backups, and workload impact before any cleanup action.
Track every recommendation with estimated savings, risk, owner, and approval status.
anti_patterns: Deleting volumes, snapshots, or instances only because they look idle.
Buying commitments before checking steady-state usage and coverage gaps.
Ignoring tags, budgets, and anomaly alerts after one cleanup project.

faq.question: Does this skill delete AWS resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example commands. Users should require explicit approval before any destructive action.

faq.question: What AWS access does it need?
faq.answer: It needs AWS CLI credentials with permissions for Cost Explorer, EC2 inventory, CloudWatch metrics, and related read-only checks.

faq.question: Can it estimate exact savings?
faq.answer: It can guide savings estimates, but exact values depend on current pricing, usage patterns, discounts, and business constraints.

faq.question: Can it analyze EC2 rightsizing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CloudWatch metric checks and instance inventory guidance for EC2 rightsizing review.

faq.question: Does it cover Reserved Instances and Savings Plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests reviewing commitment options after baseline usage and workload stability are understood.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production accounts?
faq.answer: Yes, for read-only analysis. Production changes need approvals, rollback plans, backups, and staged validation.
